newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: U.S. dollar slumps in New Zealand after G7 meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. dollar slumps in New Zealand after G7 meeting.

text.p: The U.S. dollar slumped in hectic early Monday morning New Zealand trading following the weekend's meeting of the Group of Seven major industrialised nations.
By 10.00 a.m. (2100 GMT) the dollar was at 1.6380/90 marks and 121.00/20 yen, from 1.6605/15 marks and 123.08/18 yen at New York's close on Friday. It was off its lows of 1.6350 marks and 120.30 yen.

New Zealand in the first market in the would to open in the week because of its time zone. Dealers said trading was "all over the place" in a market which is normally thin on Monday until other countries open. They said the greenback had returned to just below levels seen a week ago.

The G7 said in a statement after the meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors that the major currency misalignments it noted in its April 1995 communique had been corrected and added, as usual, that currency stability was desirable.

"They are saying okay, we've seen the appreciation, and we're happy with levels where they are now. In some ways that is bearish, because they're saying they're comfortable with the levels and they don't really want the dollar higher," a local dealer said.
He disagreed with suggestions from some U.S. financial analysts that the statement would be a green light for the dollar to move higher.

"The important thing is they are not having their hand forced, and that's what the market will look for. They've learned their lesson over the past years that intervening in foreign exchange markets is counter-productive," the dealer said.
